segments.source: Capturing a bracketed photo sequence
segments.ko: Capturing a bracketed photo sequence

segments.source: **Framework**: AVFoundation
segments.ko: **Framework**: AVFoundation

segments.source: Capture several photos at once, varying parameters like exposure duration or light sensitivity.
segments.ko: Capture several photos at once, varying parameters like exposure duration or light sensitivity.

segments.source: Overview
segments.ko: Overview

segments.source: Bracketing is a well-known photographic technique in which a sequence of shots is rapidly taken of the same scene, usually varying only in a single parameter such as aperture or shutter speed (exposure length).
segments.ko: Bracketing is a well-known photographic technique in which a sequence of shots is rapidly taken of the same scene, usually varying only in a single parameter such as aperture or shutter speed (exposure length).

segments.source: Experienced photographers use this technique to help them choose the best photos after shooting, or to apply offline post-processing that fuses multiple images together to create extended dynamic range or other special effects.
segments.ko: Experienced photographers use this technique to help them choose the best photos after shooting, or to apply offline post-processing that fuses multiple images together to create extended dynamic range or other special effects.

segments.source: In iOS, you can use [`AVCapturePhotoOutput`](avcapturephotooutput.md) and [`AVCapturePhotoBracketSettings`](avcapturephotobracketsettings.md) to automatically capture a bracket of photos for each [`capturePhoto(with:delegate:)`](avcapturephotooutput/capturephoto(with:delegate:).md) call.
segments.ko: In iOS, you can use [`AVCapturePhotoOutput`](avcapturephotooutput.md) and [`AVCapturePhotoBracketSettings`](avcapturephotobracketsettings.md) to automatically capture a bracket of photos for each [`capturePhoto(with:delegate:)`](avcapturephotooutput/capturephoto(with:delegate:).md) call.

segments.source: Once you’ve built a single-exposure camera in your app (see [`Capturing still and Live Photos`](capturing-still-and-live-photos.md)), follow these steps to add multi-image bracket support.

segments.source: Create Photo Settings and Shoot
segments.ko: Create Photo Settings and Shoot

segments.source: Instead of the [`AVCapturePhotoSettings`](avcapturephotosettings.md) object you create when shooting a single photo, to shoot a bracketed capture you’ll need an [`AVCapturePhotoBracketSettings`](avcapturephotobracketsettings.md) object.
segments.ko: Instead of the [`AVCapturePhotoSettings`](avcapturephotosettings.md) object you create when shooting a single photo, to shoot a bracketed capture you’ll need an [`AVCapturePhotoBracketSettings`](avcapturephotobracketsettings.md) object.

segments.source: This object combines the general settings that apply to all photos in the bracket with your bracket settings that specify how each photo differs from the rest of the bracket.
segments.ko: This object combines the general settings that apply to all photos in the bracket with your bracket settings that specify how each photo differs from the rest of the bracket.

segments.source: As with single-image capture, you create a photo settings object by choosing the image codec and file format for the resulting photos, but you also provide the bracket settings you’ve chosen.
segments.ko: As with single-image capture, you create a photo settings object by choosing the image codec and file format for the resulting photos, but you also provide the bracket settings you’ve chosen.

segments.source: 💡 **Tip**: Turning on [`isLensStabilizationEnabled`](avcapturephotobracketsettings/islensstabilizationenabled.md) (if supported) causes the camera to apply optical image stabilization (OIS) across the entire bracket, so that photos resulting from the bracket still line up with each other even if the device moves during capture.
segments.ko: 💡 **Tip**: Turning on [`isLensStabilizationEnabled`](avcapturephotobracketsettings/islensstabilizationenabled.md) (if supported) causes the camera to apply optical image stabilization (OIS) across the entire bracket, so that photos resulting from the bracket still line up with each other even if the device moves during capture.

segments.source: Handle Bracketed Capture Results
segments.ko: Handle Bracketed Capture Results

segments.source: The photo output calls your delegate’s [`photoOutput(_:didFinishProcessingPhoto:error:)`](avcapturephotocapturedelegate/photooutput(_:didfinishprocessingphoto:error:).md) method at least once for each exposure in the bracket, and possibly additional times depending on your capture settings.
segments.ko: The photo output calls your delegate’s [`photoOutput(_:didFinishProcessingPhoto:error:)`](avcapturephotocapturedelegate/photooutput(_:didfinishprocessingphoto:error:).md) method at least once for each exposure in the bracket, and possibly additional times depending on your capture settings.

segments.source: For example, if you request RAW+HEIF capture in a three-exposure bracket, the photo output calls your delegate’s `didFinishProcessingPhoto` method six times (2 formats × 3 exposures), providing six [`AVCapturePhoto`](avcapturephoto.md) objects.
segments.ko: For example, if you request RAW+HEIF capture in a three-exposure bracket, the photo output calls your delegate’s `didFinishProcessingPhoto` method six times (2 formats × 3 exposures), providing six [`AVCapturePhoto`](avcapturephoto.md) objects.

segments.source: To keep track of multiple results, compare the [`photoCount`](avcapturephoto/photocount.md) from each photo to the [`expectedPhotoCount`](avcaptureresolvedphotosettings/expectedphotocount.md) of your resolved settings.
segments.ko: To keep track of multiple results, compare the [`photoCount`](avcapturephoto/photocount.md) from each photo to the [`expectedPhotoCount`](avcaptureresolvedphotosettings/expectedphotocount.md) of your resolved settings.

segments.source: When those numbers are equal, you’ve received all results from the capture.
segments.ko: When those numbers are equal, you’ve received all results from the capture.
